records.c: the tune command, written by the game and read by $68F8: 0 silences the SID and stops the tune, 1 or 2 starts that tune, and anything from 3 up lets the tune playing go on. $68F8 writes $FF back before it returns (at $6E32), so a command acts once. The game writes it at $ABFB, $AC63, $B074 and $B1A0; the driver itself writes 0 at $69D9 when a pattern reaches its end-of-tune byte $FE.

the music driver, called from the play interrupt (at $8884) and from the title's (at $B20C). On command 0 it silences the SID ($6E36) and clears $74B2. On 1 or 2 it copies that tune's three order-list pointers from $7015 (six bytes a tune) to $7502 and $7505, clears each voice's note length, slide and order-list place, fetches each voice's first pattern ($6E81), resets the SID ($7001) and sets $74B2. Otherwise, while $74B2 is set, it counts each voice's three effect timers at $750C on and steps the three voices from the third down to the first ($695A), then counts the speed down ($74B4) and reloads it from $74B3 when it passes 0. Every way out writes $FF to the command.
the operand of this add, which $690D writes with twice the tune number less one, so the add makes it six times: the offset of the tune's entry in $7015

one voice's step of the driver, with X the voice (0 to 2) and $750F its SID register offset from $749D. While the speed count $74B4 is not 0 it only carries on a slide ($74E5 counts down while the note number $74AE steps down). When the count is 0 it counts the note's length $74CD down, and while the note lasts it applies the slide set by command $7E or $7F: $74E2 holds an opcode ($FE, inc, or $DE, dec), which $6972 writes over the instruction at $6975, so the note steps up or down a semitone each time. When the length runs out it reads the pattern at $A7/$A8 from the place $7508: bytes $00-$5F are notes, $60-$7F commands ($7F slide down, $7E slide up, $7D and $7C an arpeggio with a mask byte, $7B a slide to a note with a speed byte, $7A a vibrato delay byte), $80-$BF set the length (low six bits, $74CA), $C0-$DF the instrument (low five bits, times 8, $7509), $F0-$FB the speed (low four bits, $74B3), $FC the volume to 15, $FD a step of a fade (the volume from $7501, which it counts down), $FE ends the tune and $FF the pattern, which fetches the next from the order list ($6E81). A note is transposed by $74D6, gated with its instrument's waveform, envelope and pulse ($6AEA-$6B42), and then the voice's arpeggio, vibrato, slide to a note, drum and pulse sweep are applied from $6B6E on. Ends at $6E1D, where it goes on to the next voice down.
the opcode here is rewritten by $6972 from $74E2: $FE (inc $74AE,x) makes a slide step the note up a semitone, $DE (dec $74AE,x) down
the operand of this load is the instrument's first pulse width ($7024), written at $6AB4, so a new note starts its pulse there
the low byte of the drum's waveform table, written at $6B9E from the drum table at $7431
the high byte of the drum's waveform table, written at $6BA4
the low byte of the drum's frequency table, written at $6BAA

the high byte of the drum's frequency table, written at $6BB0. The drum reads one byte of each table for each of its first 15 steps ($750C counts them) and plays the frequency as a high byte with $0D added
the operand of this add is the low four bits of the slide speed, written at $6D4D
rewritten by $6EBC: $18 (clc) when the slide goes up, $38 (sec) when it goes down
rewritten by $6EBC with the opcode $6D (adc) or $ED (sbc), so this line adds or subtracts the slide's step from the low byte of the frequency
rewritten by $6EBC with the same opcode as $6D78, for the high byte of the frequency
the driver's common exit: writes $FF to the tune command $68F7, so a command is acted on once.
writes 0 to SID registers $D400-$D418, every voice's frequency, pulse, waveform and envelope, the filter and the volume.

takes the note number $74AE,x and writes its frequency from the table at $6F43 (high bytes) and $6FA2 (low bytes) to the voice's SID registers, keeping a copy in $74B8,x and $74BB,x for the vibrato and the slides.

builds a voice's arpeggio list from the mask in $7500: for each of its eight bits that is set, from bit 0 up, the semitone step from $74A3 (3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12) is added to the list at $751C, starting one place after the voice's base from $74A0, and the list is ended with $FF. Clears the voice's slide to a note ($74D9).

fetches a voice's next pattern from its order list (pointer $7502,x/$7505,x, place $74B5,x). A byte below $80 is a pattern number, looked up in the pattern table at $7121 and left in $A7/$A8 and $74C4,x/$74C7,x; $FF sends the list back to its start; any other byte from $80 up is a transpose, $40 added to it into $74D6,x (so $C0 is none and $BD is three semitones down), and the next byte is read.

sets up a slide from the note in Y to the target note $6EBD (the command $7B wrote it there): rewrites the add at $6D77 to add ($18 clc, $6D adc) or subtract ($38 sec, $ED sbc), takes the difference between the two notes' frequencies from the tables at $6F43 and $6FA2, and divides it by one more than the speed $74B3 ($6F06 on, a 16-bit division), so the slide arrives in that many steps. The step is left in $74DF/$74E0.
the slide's target note, written into this compare's operand at $6D44
the operand of this add is the low four bits of the slide speed, written at $6D50
the high bytes of the notes' SID frequencies, one per note number, read with the low bytes at $6FA2
the note frequency table's high bytes read one note on, by the vibrato at $6C6D to find a semitone's difference
the low bytes of the notes' SID frequencies, beside the high bytes at $6F43
the note frequency table's low bytes read one note on, by the vibrato at $6C63

clears the SID ($6E36), sets the volume to 15 with the filter on the low pass ($D418 = $5F), and clears the speed count $74B4, the playing flag $74B2 and the filter resonance $D417. Called when a tune starts ($693C).
the two tunes, six bytes each: the addresses of the three voices' order lists, low byte then high. Tune 1's are $715F, $7174 and $718E, tune 2's $71A0, $71AB and $71BA.

32 instruments of eight bytes, picked by a pattern's $C0-$DF byte: the waveform with its gate ($7021), attack and decay ($7022), sustain and release ($7023), the pulse width's first value ($7024), the drum and arpeggio byte ($7025: the low four bits name a drum at $7431, bit 4 plays it as notes), the pulse sweep's step ($7026), an arpeggio mask ($7027) and flags ($7028: bit 0 a drum, bit 1 a short slide up, bit 2 an eight-bit pulse sweep, bit 3 a drum played by $6C04, bit 7 the pulse width kept from note to note)

an instrument's eighth byte, its flags: bit 0 a drum, bit 1 a short slide up at the note's start, bit 2 an eight-bit pulse sweep, bit 3 a drum played as a waveform (at $6C04), bit 7 the pulse width kept from note to note

the sound effect asked for on the first voice, $FF for none; $753D and $753E are the second and third voices'. $756A starts it and writes $FF back. The first two are written only together, at $AC58; the third at $8D89, $958B, $95DB, $A9E5, $AA8E and $AC5E.

the sound effects' step, called from the play interrupt (at $888A): sets the volume to 15 ($7548), then runs the effects player ($756A).
sets the SID's volume to 15 with the filter off ($D418 = $0F).
stops every sound effect: clears $7751-$7753 and $7760-$7762, and writes 0 to the SID's voice registers $D400-$D412.
the sound effects player, for the three voices from the third down. Starts an effect asked for in $753C,x ($758A), then steps one that is playing ($7663). Saves and restores X and Y.

starts sound effect A on voice X: copies its 16-byte record from $7778 + 16 * A into the voice's variables at $772A-$776F, writes $FF to the request, and writes the record's pulse, envelope, frequency and waveform to the voice's SID registers ($775D,x is its offset). A record's last byte, the repeats, of $FF makes the effect repeat until it is stopped ($7760).

one step of the effect on voice X. While its time $7748 lasts it moves the frequency by the step $773F/$7742 by its mode ($773C: 1 up, 2 down, 3 swapping between the two frequencies each step, 0 none). When the time runs out it starts the effect again from its first frequency while repeats are left ($7736), or else lets the gate go and counts the release ($776F) down, after which the effect is over. A bug: at $76FC it writes the sustain and release with X, the voice number, as the index, not with Y, its register offset, so for the second and third voices the byte lands in $D407 and $D408, the second voice's frequency.
the low byte of each voice's effect frequency as it moves

the 26 sound effects, 16 bytes each: the first frequency (two bytes), the step (two), the mode, the time, the waveform, the attack and decay, the sustain and release, the pulse width, four bytes copied to $7763-$776C, one byte not read, and the repeats ($FF for for ever)
the text CBM80000, nine bytes in front of the entry; nothing reads it
the game's entry, as BASIC's SYS 32777 reaches it: sets $01 to $36 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF, the I/O and the KERNAL in) and falls into the main loop at $800D.

the game's outer loop. The title ($AF23) runs until a fire button starts a game; then the game is set up ($82E3) and each city is set up ($82EC) and played, one pass at a time: $8065 does each pass's frame work and $89B2 moves the monsters and everything else. When a pass ends with both monsters' $80E9 at 0 the game is over: $804B sets $8032 to 1 and runs passes of $8065 and $89B5 (everything but the monsters) until $8032 reaches $28, then goes back to the title. When $802E is set, or $8032 has reached $14, the city is over: $ABB7 runs and the city count $803E goes on (from 5 back to 1) to the next city. Otherwise the next pass starts at $8019. Never returns.
the operand of this load, cleared at $84F9 and written in play: when it is not 0 after $89B2 returns, the city is over
the operand of this compare's load, cleared at $84FC and written in play: $14 after $89B2 ends the city, and the game-over loop at $8050 runs until it reaches $28
the number of the city in the run, 1 to 5, kept as the operand of this load: $8037 counts it on after each city and puts it back to 1 after 5. $8444 picks the next city with it.

the work of one pass of play before the monsters move: waits for line $C8 ($B733), clears $3E7F and runs $A437, waits a frame, waits for line $C8, then with $3E7F at 1 runs $8942 (the buildings' timers), with $3E7F at 2 restores marked cells of the screen ($8970), animates the characters ($B463) and waits a frame. Called twice from the main loop.
sets up a new game: installs the play interrupt ($8426), the video chip's bank and modes ($8301) and the monsters ($8326).
sets up the next city with the screen off ($B746): picks it ($8444), builds it ($853E), then $9772, $9925 and $9B4F, and turns the screen on ($B752).
puts the video chip in bank 3 ($DD00 = $94), the screen at $C800 and the characters at $C000 ($D018 = $20), turns the screen on ($D011 bit 4) and multicolour on, with 40 columns ($D016).

sets up the monsters for a new game: clears both monsters' health and the counts at $80E7 and $80E8, sets the city count $803E to 1, picks the first city type at random, 1 or 2 ($B75E with 2, plus 1, into $80A8), fills the top two rows of the screen with character $FA, and sets up the lizard ($8368) if its fire started the game ($80EB) and the ogre ($83B2) if its did ($80EC).
1 while the lizard has not been set up in this game; $8368 sets it up once and clears it
1 while the ogre has not been set up in this game; $83B2 clears it

sets up the lizard, once a game ($8366): points its score digits at $C80B and its two bars at $C805 and $C82D (writing them into the code at $8413, $841D and $8420), marks the ends of the bars, sets its start position from the tables at $B69A and $B6A5 by the city type, and gives it its health and power ($83F9). Called at the start of a game and from play ($8A98), so the other monster can join a game that is on.
sets up the ogre as $8368 does the lizard, with its score at $C815 and its bars at $C81D and $C845, and its start position from $B6B0 and $B6BB.

gives monster X (0 the lizard, 1 the ogre) $20 health ($80E9,x) and $20 power ($80ED,x), sets $8215,x to 8 and clears $80E7,x and $8213,x, then writes its seven score digits as $F0 (0 in the heavy digits) and its two bars of five cells as $FE, through the addresses $8368 or $83B2 wrote into these stores.
the low byte of the score digits' address, written by $8368 or $83B2
the high byte of the score digits' address

the high byte of the second bar's address
installs the play interrupt, $8810 on line 0 ($B6E9).
the city types $8444 picks from, 21 bytes: four times the city count plus a random number index it

picks the next city and resets play for it: the city type ($80A8) is the byte of $842F at four times the city count ($803E) plus a byte of the table at $9C12, indexed by a counter $A91E that it counts on (and the title counts on every frame); turns all eight sprites on, multicoloured, in front and unexpanded; and clears or sets play's variables for a new city (positions, counts, the sprite colours and the tables at $821F and $8280-$82AD).

builds the city of type $80A8 on the screen. Fills the character colours at $A2A1 with the city's colour from $87EF and copies the first 128 from the city's data (addresses at $82CF and $82D9); saves the top two rows of the screen to $9D12; copies the next kilobyte of the data to the character set at $C000; copies 62 characters from the city's table (addresses at $B691 and $B688) to $C590; unpacks the screen from the data into $C828 up to $CBFF (a byte with bit 7 set repeats the next byte its low seven bits plus one times, any other copies that many bytes plus one as they are); keeps a copy of the screen at $7918; sets the border and background colours from $B6D7, $B5D7, $B5E1 and $B5EB. Unless $8691 is set it then sets the city's values ($8244-$8247 from $8248-$8262, $A9A3 from $B6C6), builds characters $96 and $9B-$9D from the city's ($C4B0-$C4EF), the monsters' start positions, and six buildings from $B5F5, $B626 and $B657 (drawn by $93F0). Last it puts the top two rows back, colours the screen from $A2A1 character by character, colours the panel, gives the fourth city type its extra characters at $C9F3-$CA1C, and sets $9926 and $9B4A to 13 for the second city type and 5 for the others.

the play interrupt on line 0, the first band of sprites. counts down the timers ($8280,x) of the buildings that stand ($82A8,x clear) and are burning or falling ($8298,x or $8290,x set), from the sixth down; the first whose count reaches 0 has its next stage drawn ($93F0) and its count reloaded with what that returns, and the rest wait for a later pass. Then, if $8032 is not 0, counts it on.
looks at screen rows 7 to 24 for character $AF, a mark the game leaves on a cell for one pass, and puts back each one it finds from the city's copy of the screen at $7918, with its colour from $A2A1.
one pass of play: the monsters ($89D6), then the rest ($89B5).

everything in a pass of play but the monsters: $9772, $9925, $9B4F, $A43D; stores a random number from 1 to 4 in the table at $9C12 at the place $A91E, which the next city's choice and other random choices read; and adds the monsters' points owed to their scores ($93AE).
moves the lizard (X = 0), then the ogre (X = 1), with $89E0.

one monster's pass, X the monster (0 the lizard, 1 the ogre). First sets $8264 when the position at $80B1/$80B2 is within 20 pixels across of the pair of sprites at $8244/$8245 and 45 to 58 lines above it, and $8265 the same for $80B3/$80B4. While its punch ($82B9,x), flame ($82BB,x) or eating ($82BF,x) timer runs, it only counts that on ($912E, $9125, $9111). Otherwise it reads its joystick (lda $DC00,x: port 2 for the lizard, port 1 for the ogre) into $8A61. If its $80E9,x is 0 (not in the game), fire joins it ($8368 or $83B2). If $80E9,x is not $20 it is dying: the count goes down a pass, with sound $10, and the animation steps every eight. Otherwise fire acts ($8D07) and up, down, left and right walk ($8ACD, $8B34, $8BA4, $8C30); with nothing pressed it only counts $A91E on.
the monster's joystick bits, written into this load's operand at $8A46: 0 for pressed, bit 0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right, 4 fire

up: walks into the screen. Faces away (0) and moves up a row every second pass, while the cells it would move onto are walkable (from $95 up, or the city's character in $A9A3) and the other monster is not just ahead.
down: walks out of the screen, to row $14 at most, in the same way (facing 8).
left: walks left to column 1 at most, half a cell a pass, while the cells there are walkable (facing $0C).
right: walks right to column $23 at most (facing 4).
the end of a step: counts the monster's animation frame $8213,x on, 0 to 3.
three bytes no code reaches, jmp $8BA4
the screen address of monster X's place, $C800 + 40 times (its row $80AF,x less 1) + its column $80AB,x, in $FB/$FC. Fifteen callers.

fire. With a direction it is a punch, with the stick in the middle a flame ($914D set, the flame timer $82BB,x to 6); first it eats what is in reach ($914E). A flame within three columns and a row of the other monster hurts it ($931E) and scores 1; one while $8264,x is set (with $8242 of 7 or more) scores 1, takes 1 from $8242, asks for sound 2 on the third voice and counts $8240 round 1 to 4. Then by the direction, or for a flame the way the monster faces, it goes to the building above ($8DB1), below ($8E75), to the left ($8F2C) or to the right ($901C).

fire up, or a flame facing up: looks for a standing building just above the monster within its width. A punch, while the monster has punching power ($80ED,x), knocks a hole in it ($B44A), starts it falling ($8290,x) and scores 10; a flame sets it alight ($9730, then $94FF every second pass) and scores 1.
fire down, or a flame facing down: the same for a building just below.
fire left, or a flame facing left: the same for a building to the left; a punch at nothing with power left counts $82B7,x.
the height of the building less one, written into this compare's operand at $8F6D
nine bytes no code reaches: sta $8298,x, ldx $80A6, rts
fire right, or a flame facing right: the same for a building to the right.
the height of the building less one, written into this compare's operand at $904F

the end of a punch or a flame: keeps where it was aimed in $82BD,x; for a flame asks for sound 3 and moves the animation to the flame frames; for a punch starts the punch timer ($82B9,x = 8), stops the monster's sound and takes a cell of punching power ($92D6).
nine bytes no code reaches, the same as those at $8FEB
the eating timer: counts it down and scores 1 when it runs out
1 while the fire being handled is a flame, 0 for a punch; set at $8D36

before a punch or a flame: if one of the eight things at $821F (people) is within four columns and two or three rows above the monster, it is taken ($821F,y = 2) and eaten: the eating timer ($82BF,x = 6), sound $0D, the eating frames, and the punch or flame is dropped. Otherwise it looks at the four cells in each of four rows around the monster for a pickup ($91C4).

what the character at ($FB),Y gives: $82 sets the punching power ($80ED,x = 1) and adds a cell to the second bar; $86 adds a cell to the first bar; $8A hurts the monster eight times ($931E); $8E sets $9687 to 2, asks for sound 8, scores 3 and counts $8032 on. Each taken leaves the mark $AF on its four cells ($92B9), which $8970 puts back.
adds to a bar: the cell at ($FB) + the bar's place ($9342) is made full ($FE) and what it held moves to the next cell, up to the fifth.
a punch spends a cell of punching power: takes one from the monster's second bar ($938D on $C82D or $C845), and when the bar is empty clears $80ED,x, so a punch does nothing more.

hurts monster X: sets $821D,x and takes one from its first bar ($938D on $C805 or $C81D). For the ogre, when the bar is empty and it is in the game ($80E9,x = $20), its count starts down (dying) and its score goes to the best ($B3CF). For the lizard the code differs: the bar's place is set back to the first cell (lda #$00 where the ogre's keeps $9342) and the test of the empty bar is lda #$00, so the lizard's bar never empties past its first cell and the lizard never starts to die from a hurt; the code at $934A that would start it is reached by nothing. Saves $FB/$FC, X and Y.
the place in a bar that $938D and $9284 work on, 0 to 4
set by $938D when the bar it takes from is empty
takes one from the bar at ($FB), at the place A: the cells go from $FE (full) down to $FA (empty); when the cell is empty it moves the place back one, and when the first cell is empty sets $9347.
adds a point the monsters are owed ($80E7, $80E8) to each one's score, one a pass: the score's tens digit is counted on ($93D1), so a point is 10 on the screen.
counts on the score digit at ($FB)+5, carrying into the digits to its left; the digits are the heavy ones, $F0-$F9.

draws the next stage of building X, with its size from $827E/$827F and its screen place from $9730: a standing building is redrawn from its graphic; a burning one ($8290,x from 1 to 4) gets the next of its flame pictures (the characters from $82B0), with a random chance from $9C12 of going out; at stage 5 it falls ($82A0,x); a fallen one ($8298,x) is cleared away ($95D9). the flame picture's first character, written at $9496 from $82B0

a flame on building X: with a random chance from $9C12 lets one of the eight people at $821F run out of it (at a random column of the building, at its foot), then works its way down the building a row ($82A0,x) and scatters one to three rubble characters ($B0) on that row; when the rows run out the building falls ($8298,x). Asks for sound $0B on the third voice and sets the building's timer to 5.

installs a raster interrupt: A is its line, X and Y the handler's address. Turns the video chip's interrupts off, writes the line and the vector $0314, clears bit 8 of the line in $D011, turns CIA 1's interrupts and timer A off, acknowledges and enables the raster interrupt and clears I.
the end of every raster handler: writes the next handler (X and Y) to $0314 and its line (A) to $D012, acknowledges the interrupt, pulls Y, X and A as the KERNAL's entry pushed them and returns.
waits for the raster to reach line 256 (bit 7 of $D011 set), then to leave the bottom of the screen, so it returns as the next frame starts.
waits until the raster reaches line A: writes A into its own compare at $B73A and waits while $D012 is less.
the line $B733 waits for, written into the compare's operand at $B733
makes A positive if the flags the caller's last instruction left say it is negative: if N is set it negates A (two's complement). Eight callers.
waits for the next frame and blanks the screen ($D011 bit 4 off).
waits for the next frame and turns the screen on ($D011 bit 4).

a random number from 0 to A less one: steps the shift register at $B7B0-$B7B3 eight times ($B794), so its top byte is eight new bits, and multiplies that by A, returning the high byte of the product. X is kept. Five callers.

steps the 32-bit shift register $B7B0-$B7B3 one bit: the new bit is bits 3 and 6 of its top byte, exclusive-ored (and #$48, adc #$38 and two shifts bring it to the carry), rotated in at the bottom. Returns the top byte.
